rule: Remember state, not every time state became true.

completion.resolution: first write wins at ingest (Statewave idempotency)

preference.resolution: claim supersession at compile; latest by claim valid_from, then created_at, then memory id

scenarios.BS01: 1000 observations of one completion -> 1 durable record, completed=true
scenarios.BS02: 4 preference changes -> active value CONCISE; 4 episodes, 1 active claim
scenarios.BS03: 200 distinct completion keys -> 200 records, 200 features in profile
scenarios.BS04: newest of 150 records reachable via newest_first
scenarios.BS07: build-1 completion does not mark build-2 complete
scenarios.BS10: reset leaves nothing and resurrects nothing
scenarios.BS11: a retried write is one record
scenarios.BS12: retry deduplicates; a new value supersedes — different mechanisms, both held
scenarios.BS13: read failure -> absence, REMOTE_DEGRADED, nothing thrown
scenarios.BS15: 26 records swept, 0 forbidden values (instances, secrets, emails, questions, UI text)
scenarios.BS16: active invoice-adjacent state; unsupported question still refused
scenarios.BS17: remembered delete completion adds no Delete action
scenarios.BS19: same-instant competing writes -> arbitrary but stable winner (documented tie)
scenarios.combined: 504 writes -> 5 durable episodes -> 2 events read (completed=true, CONCISE)

limitations: preference supersession requires a tenant id and a host-registered claim key; without both, Guide falls back to replaying preference episodes (correct, unbounded)
physical episode history grows with distinct facts plus preference changes; superseded memory rows are retained by Statewave as history
the SDK does not yet expose status=active (unpublished); the adapter filters the documented status field client-side
same-instant competing preference writes resolve arbitrarily but stably; "latest" is claim valid_from, then created_at, then memory id
